risk_if_not_implemented: Without Compensating Controls for Quantum-Vulnerable Systems, sensitive data with long confidentiality lifetimes remains protected only by quantum-vulnerable cryptography, exposing it to future decryption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Long-Term Confidentiality Loss from Cryptographic Obsolescence (R-IP-1), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL) (MT-28), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_1.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Compensating Controls for Quantum-Vulnerable Systems (QTS-04.2) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Least Privilege
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize the concept of least privilege, allowing only authorized access to processes necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational business functions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Least Privilege (IAC-30) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Compensating Controls for Quantum-Vulnerable Systems (QTS-04.2) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
